title: Spoyrt
description: Ten mini stories about sport and exercise: a Saturday football match, a tennis lesson, a sports day, a mountain run, food for players, languages at a table tennis club, a sports science lab, cycling in Iceland, a referendum on a swimming pool and an archery club at Castle Rushen.

lessons.title: Gamman Jesarn
lessons.summary: Natalie Rafferty, a sports presenter on Manx TV, covers a Saturday football match in Douglas: the goalkeeper Darren Lowery catches the ball on his chest, the referee stops the game in a storm for the players' safety, adverts fill the break, and Natalie writes an article about Douglas's seventh win.
lessons.text:
She çhebbeyder spoyrt ee Natalie Rafferty. T'ee gobbraghey er y çhellveeish ayns Doolish. Dagh Jesarn, t'ee loayrt mychione ny gammanyn bluckan-coshey. Jesarn shoh, va gamman mooar ayn: Doolish noi Rhumsaa. Va Doolish er chosney shey gammanyn 'sy vlein shoh, as v'ad laccal y shiaghtoo gamman y chosney.

Hie Natalie dys y gamman ayns y gleashtan eck. Va ram gleashtanyn er y raad, as v'ee anmagh. Tra v'ee er roshtyn, va ny cloiederyn çheet magh.

Va Darren Lowery ayns y goal son Doolish. Ayns y chied lieh, haink y bluckan huggey dy tappee. Ren Darren y bluckan y ghlackey er e chleeau. “Shen glackey feer vie!” dooyrt Natalie er y çhellveeish. Keayrt as keayrt, va'n bluckan glackit ec Darren.

Eisht haink fliaghey trome as geay lajer. Cha row ny cloiederyn abyl fakin y bluckan. Ren y briw y gamman y scuirr. “Ta sauçhey ny cloiederyn ny smoo scanshoil na'n gamman,” dooyrt eh. Scuirr ny cloiederyn, as hie ad stiagh.

Choud as va'n gamman scuirrit, va soilsheenyn er y çhellveeish. Va soilsheen ayn mychione gleashtan noa, as soilsheen elley mychione bee son cloiederyn. “Ta ny soilsheenyn shoh ny share na'n emshir!” dooyrt Natalie.

Lurg lieh oor, scuirr y fliaghey. Haink ny cloiederyn magh reesht. Ayns y nah lieh, hooar Doolish un goal, as cha dooar Rhumsaa goal erbee. Va'n shiaghtoo gamman cosnit ec Doolish.

'Syn oie, screeu Natalie art mychione y ghamman son y pabyr-naight. Screeu ee mychione y fliaghey, mychione sauçhey ny cloiederyn, as mychione Darren as y bluckan er e chleeau. Va'n art mie, as ren ram sleih lhaih eh.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ee Natalie Rafferty?
She çhebbeyder spoyrt ee er y çhellveeish.
Cre'n laa va'n gamman?
Va'n gamman Jesarn.
Cre'n fa ren y briw y gamman y scuirr?
Ren eh y gamman y scuirr son sauçhey ny cloiederyn.
Cre va er y çhellveeish choud as va'n gamman scuirrit?
Va soilsheenyn er y çhellveeish.
Cre screeu Natalie 'syn oie?
Screeu ee art mychione y ghamman.

lessons.title: Yn leddogeyr aeg
lessons.summary: Iona Kegeen, a fourteen-year-old tennis player, has a lesson with her coach Graham Cubbin, who praises her ability and gives her an example; she wears a white headband and plays with new, expensive balls of good quality, drinks water in the heat, wins her match and shows respect to the other player.
lessons.text:
Ta Iona Kegeen kiare bleeaney jeig d'eash, as she leddogeyr aeg ee. Dagh Jeheiney lurg y scoill, t'ee goll dys lessoon. Ta'n ynseyder eck, Graham Cubbin, ny shenn leddogeyr. V'eh cloie ayns Sostyn as ayns Nerin tra v'eh aeg.

'Sy lessoon shoh, ren Graham jeeaghyn er ablid Iona. “Ta ablid vie ayd,” dooyrt eh. “T'ou roie dy tappee, as t'ou cur yn bluckan harrish dy lajer. Agh lhisagh oo smooinaghtyn roish my ver oo yn bluckan.”

Va feysht ec Iona. “Cre'n aght ta mee smooinaghtyn as mee roie?” “Shen feysht mie,” dooyrt Graham. “Shoh sambyl. Jeeagh er y leddogeyr elley. My t'eh faggys da'n mean, cur yn bluckan dys y jerrey. My t'eh ec y jerrey, cur yn bluckan faggys da'n mean.” Va'n sambyl aashagh dy hoiggal.

Va rimmeig vane mygeayrt kione Iona, as rimmeig ghorrym mygeayrt e laue. Chionnee e moir bluckanyn noa j'ee. “Va ny bluckanyn shoh deyr,” dooyrt e moir, “agh ta quallid vie oc.” Ta quallid scanshoil son leddogeyr. Cha nel bluckanyn deyr kinjagh mie, agh ta bluckanyn jeh quallid vie goll dy jeeragh.

Lurg y lessoon, va gamman ec Iona noi leddogeyr veih Pheeil. Va'n emshir feer çheh. “Jean ushtey y iu eddyr ny ayrnyn,” dooyrt Graham. Ren Iona ushtey y iu dy mennick. Cha ren ee y chied ayrn y chosney, agh ren ee cooinaghtyn er y lessoon as er sambyl Graham. Ren ee smooinaghtyn roish dagh bluckan, as ren ee y daa ayrn elley y chosney.

Ec y jerrey, hug Iona e laue da'n leddogeyr elley. “Ta ammys ayd er y leddogeyr elley,” dooyrt Graham. “Ta ammys cho scanshoil as cosney.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n eash ta Iona?
T'ee kiare bleeaney jeig d'eash.
Quoi eh Graham Cubbin?
She ynseyder eh, as shenn leddogeyr.
Cre va mygeayrt kione Iona?
Va rimmeig vane mygeayrt e kione.
Cre dooyrt e moir mychione ny bluckanyn?
Dooyrt ee dy row ad deyr, agh dy vel quallid vie oc.
Cre ren Iona eddyr ny ayrnyn?
Ren ee ushtey y iu.

lessons.title: Laa spoyrt ayns Doolish
lessons.summary: At a sports day in Douglas, Nerys Caveen, a shot-put thrower who has been strengthening her arms, throws eleven metres, and her brother Joel turns on the horizontal bar with arms stretched out, keeping his body in one plane around the bar as an axis; his double turn ties with a boy from Ramsey, and the judges cannot tell them apart.
lessons.text:
Ta Nerys Caveen ny ceaueyder: t'ee ceau clagh trome ayns gammanyn spoyrt. Ta'n braar eck, Joel, jannoo spoyrt er y vaare co-chruinnagh, baare jiarn ard ta lhie co-chruinnagh harrish y laare.

Roish y laa spoyrt mooar ayns Doolish, v'ad gobbraghey dy chrooaght. Ren Nerys e laueyn y niartaghey 'sy shamyr spoyrt. V'ee troggal jiarn trome dagh laa. “Ayns un vee, ta mee troggal mysh thunney dy yiarn,” dooyrt ee rish Joel. “Thunney!” dooyrt Joel. “She red feer trome eh thunney.” Ren Joel e chorp y niartaghey myrgeddin.

Er y laa spoyrt, va Nerys hoshiaght. Cheau ee y clagh nuy meadaryn. Eisht cheau ee eh jeih meadaryn. Ec y jerrey, cheau ee eh 11 meadaryn. Cha row ceaueyder elley abyl ceau ny smoo na jeih meadaryn, as myr shen ren Nerys cosney.

Eisht va Joel er y vaare co-chruinnagh. Hug eh e chorp seose, as eisht ren eh çhyndaa mygeayrt y vaare lesh e laueyn sheeynt as e chassyn sheeynt. “Ta'n baare myr essyl,” dooyrt yn ynseyder echey rish Nerys. “Ta Joel çhyndaa mygeayrt yn essyl myr queeyl.”

Lhisagh y corp ve jeeragh, as lhisagh ny laueyn as ny cassyn ve ayns yn un plaaney. My ta cass ayns plaaney elley, ta ny briwnyn goaill point ersooyl. Va corp Joel jeeragh, as cha daink cass erbee magh ass y plaaney.

Ec y jerrey, ren Joel çhyndaa dooblit: ren eh çhyndaa daa cheayrt 'syn aer roish my haink eh sheese er y laare. Cha row guilley elley abyl çhyndaa dooblit y yannoo, agh un ghuilley veih Rhumsaa.

Va'n un earroo ec Joel as ec y guilley veih Rhumsaa. Cha row ny briwnyn abyl geddyr-scarrey yn daa ghuilley. “Cha nod shin geddyr-scarrey eddyr y daa ghuilley,” dooyrt y briw. “Ta'n daa ghuilley er chosney.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Nerys ceau?
T'ee ceau clagh trome.
Cre wheesh dy yiarn ta Nerys troggal ayns un vee?
T'ee troggal mysh thunney dy yiarn.
Cre cho foddey cheau ee y clagh ec y jerrey?
Cheau ee eh 11 meadaryn.
Cre ta Joel jannoo er y vaare co-chruinnagh?
T'eh çhyndaa mygeayrt y vaare lesh e laueyn sheeynt.
Cre'n fa va'n daa ghuilley er chosney?
Cha row ny briwnyn abyl geddyr-scarrey yn daa ghuilley.

lessons.title: Roie er ny sleityn
lessons.summary: On an autumn Saturday Kirsten Lewthwaite runs from Laxey through a pine wood where worms lie on the wet path, up a rocky track among tawny ferns with small leaflets and red stems, past a raven on a bare summit and wild deer, down to a little croft with a dun horse, and along the sand of the beach.
lessons.text:
Ta Kirsten Lewthwaite cummal ayns Laksaa, as s'mie lhee roie 'sy cheyll as er ny sleityn. 'Sy fouyr, ta'n aer feayr as glen, as ta ny duillagyn jiarg as buigh.

Moghrey Jesarn, hie Kirsten magh. Hoshiaght, roie ee trooid keyll juys. Ta ny biljyn juys glass 'sy gheurey as 'sy tourey, as va soar millish jeu. Va'n raad fliugh lurg y fliaghey, as va beishteigyn er y raad. Va ny beishteigyn mooar as jiarg-dhone. Ren Kirsten shooyl son tammylt, er-y-fa nagh row ee laccal goll er ny beishteigyn.

Eisht roie ee seose raad creggagh. Ta roie er raad creggagh doillee: ta clagh ayns dagh boayl. Mygeayrt y raad, va lossreeyn ouyr: va ny duillagyn oc ouyr as dhone 'sy fouyr. Ren Kirsten jeeaghyn er lus jeu. Va ram duillageenyn beggey er dagh duillag, as va sthole jiarg ec y lus. Va'n sthole lajer ayns y gheay.

Er mullagh y slieau, va'n thalloo lhoamey. Cha row billey erbee er y slieau lhoamey, agh va feeagh mooar doo ny hoie er clagh. Ren y feeagh eam ard, as hie eh ersooyl er y gheay. Ta ny feeaghyn cummal er ny sleityn ard 'syn ellan.

Faggys da'n mullagh, honnick Kirsten feeaih oaldey. Ta ny feeaih oaldey cummal er ny sleityn shoh, agh cha nel ad laccal ve faggys da sleih. Roie ny feeaih oaldey ersooyl.

Roie Kirsten sheese gys croit veg. Va thie beg bane er y chroit, as va cabbyl ouyr 'sy vagher. Va shenn ven ec thie y chroit. “Moghrey mie,” dooyrt ee. “Vel oo laccal ushtey?” Ren Kirsten ushtey y iu.

Ec y jerrey, roie Kirsten er y traie. Va'n geinnagh bog as fliugh. Ta roie er geinnagh doillee, agh ta'n geinnagh mie son ny cassyn.

Feyshtyn:
Raad roie Kirsten hoshiaght?
Roie ee trooid keyll juys.
Cre va er y raad fliugh?
Va beishteigyn er y raad.
Cre va er dagh duillag jeh'n lus?
Va duillageenyn beggey er dagh duillag.
Cre honnick Kirsten er y slieau lhoamey?
Honnick ee feeagh mooar doo.
Cre va 'sy vagher ec y chroit?
Va cabbyl ouyr 'sy vagher.

lessons.title: Bee son skimmee
lessons.summary: Aaron Doyle, a big eater on a Ramsey football team, asks the food adviser Leanne Corrie what to eat: flakes with berries he picks himself, olive oil, organic vegetables, cabbage cut thin, nuts, and sour milk with good microbes; he cooks fish and turns off the cooker before it burns.
lessons.text:
Ta Aaron Doyle ayns skimmee bluckan-coshey ayns Rhumsaa. She eeder mooar eh: t'eh gee feill as ooylyn dagh laa. Agh 'sy vlein shoh, v'eh laccal bee share y ee son spoyrt. Hie eh dys Leanne Corrie, ben ta cur coyrle mychione bee da cloiederyn.

“She eeder mooar mee,” dooyrt Aaron. “Cre lhisagh mee y ee?” “She red mie eh dy ve ny eeder mooar,” dooyrt Leanne, “my t'ou gee bee mie.”

“'Sy voghrey, ee floagyn,” dooyrt ee. “Ta floagyn lesh bainney mie son bree. Cur messyn er ny floagyn.” Ayns y fouyr, ta berrishyn dooie er ny biljyn beggey. Hie Aaron magh dy teiy berrishyn. Ren eh cappan dy verrishyn y heiy, as hug eh ad er ny floagyn echey.

“Jean ymmyd jeh ooill olive,” dooyrt Leanne. “Ta ooill olive mie son y chree. Cur ooill olive er ny lossreeyn.” Dooyrt ee myrgeddin dy vel lossreeyn orgaanagh mie. Ta lossreeyn orgaanagh ny smoo deyr, agh cha nel ad aasit lesh kemmigyn. Chionnee Aaron lossreeyn orgaanagh 'sy vargey.

Chionnee eh cabbash mooar glass. Va Aaron giarey yn cabbash ayns peeshyn beggey, as hug eh ooill olive er. Ta giarey cabbash aashagh. “Ta cabbash mie son y corp,” dooyrt Leanne.

“As cro?” dooyrt Aaron. “Ta cro mie,” dooyrt Leanne. “Ee daa ny tree croyn eddyr bee. Ta bree ayns ny croyn.” Va fys ec Aaron dy vel croyn mie lesh ooylyn.

“Iu bainney geayr,” dooyrt Leanne. “Ta mynvioee mie ayns y bainney geayr. Ta ny mynvioee shen mie son y volg.” Cha row fys ec Aaron dy row mynvioagh mie ayn. “Ta ram drogh vynvioee ayn,” dooyrt Leanne, “agh ta ram mynvioee mie myrgeddin.”

'Syn oie, hug Aaron eeast er yn aile. Lurg tammylt, ren eh yn aile y vooghey. Cha row yn eeast doo: va'n eeast mie. Dooyrt e voir: “Ren oo yn aile y vooghey ec y traa kiart!”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ee Leanne Corrie?
She ben ee ta cur coyrle mychione bee da cloiederyn.
Cre ta Aaron gee 'sy voghrey nish?
T'eh gee floagyn lesh berrishyn.
Cre'n fa ta lossreeyn orgaanagh mie?
Cha nel ad aasit lesh kemmigyn.
Cre ren Aaron lesh y cabbash?
Va Aaron giarey yn cabbash ayns peeshyn beggey.
Cre ren eh lurg tammylt?
Ren eh yn aile y vooghey.

lessons.title: Çhengaghyn 'sy chlub
lessons.summary: At a sports club near Douglas the coach Mei Zhou from Beijing and the player Willow Hayes swap languages after training: Mei explains pinyin and the four tones of Chinese, and Willow, who had her education in Manx, explains nasal and voiced sounds, the genitive (mooir, marrey) and inflected verb forms; after almost a year they hold a conversation in each language.
lessons.text:
Ta club spoyrt er gerrey da Doolish. Ta'n club er gerrey da'n traie, as ta ram sleih aegey cloie spoyrt ayn. She Mei Zhou yn ynseyder. Haink ee veih Beijing gys Ellan Vannin roish daa vlein.

Lurg y traenal, ta Mei as Willow Hayes, cloieder aeg, ynsaghey çhengaghyn y cheilley. Ta Mei ynsaghey Sheenish da Willow, as ta Willow ynsaghey Gaelg da Mei.

“Ta Sheenish screeuit lesh cowraghyn,” dooyrt Mei, “agh ta shin ynsaghey eh lesh pinyin. Ta pinyin screeu ny focklyn lesh lettyryn myr ny lettyryn Gaelg.” Hug ee pabyr da Willow lesh focklyn ayns pinyin.

“Ta kiare toanyn ayns Sheenish,” dooyrt Mei. “Ta un fockle ayn ta 'moir' lesh un toan, as 'cabbyl' lesh toan elley.” Ren Willow eab dy ghra ny kiare toanyn. Va'n toan jerrinagh doillee.

Eisht va traa Willow. Va edjaghys ayns Gaelg ec Willow: hie ee dys bunscoill raad ta ooilley ny lessoonyn ayns Gaelg. “Lurg yn edjaghys shen, ta Gaelg aashagh dou,” dooyrt ee.

“Ta sheeanyn stronnagh ayns Gaelg,” dooyrt Willow. “Ta'n chied sheean ayns 'moir' as 'naight' stronnagh: ta'n aer goll magh ass y stroin.” “Ta sheeanyn stronnagh ayns Sheenish myrgeddin,” dooyrt Mei.

“Ta'n chied sheean ayns 'gaue' cronnaneagh, agh cha nel y chied sheean ayns 'cass' cronnaneagh,” dooyrt Willow. “Cur dty laue er dty scoarnagh. Ta'n scoarnagh gleashaghey lesh sheean cronnaneagh.”

“Nish, y cummey gienneydagh,” dooyrt Willow. “Ta 'mooir' çheet dy ve 'marrey' ayns y cummey gienneydagh: 'eeast marrey'.” Va'n cummey gienneydagh noa da Mei.

“As ta cummaghyn yn-filleydagh ec ny breearyn Gaelg,” dooyrt Willow. “She cummaghyn yn-filleydagh jeh 'goll' ad 'hie' as 'hed'.” “Cha nel cummaghyn yn-filleydagh ec breearyn Sheenish,” dooyrt Mei.

Lurg bunnys blein, va coloayrtys ec Mei as Willow ayns Gaelg, as coloayrtys elley ayns Sheenish. V'ad loayrt bunnys lieh oor ayns dagh çhengey. “She coloayrtys feer vie v'ayn!” dooyrt Mei.

Feyshtyn:
Raad ta'n club?
T'eh er gerrey da Doolish, er gerrey da'n traie.
Cre ta pinyin?
Ta pinyin screeu Sheenish lesh lettyryn.
Cre'n earroo dy toanyn ta ayns Sheenish?
Ta kiare toanyn ayns Sheenish.
Cre'n edjaghys v'ec Willow?
Va edjaghys ayns Gaelg eck.
Cre ta 'mooir' ayns y cummey gienneydagh?
She 'marrey' eh.
Cre va ec Mei as Willow lurg bunnys blein?
Va coloayrtys oc ayns Gaelg as ayns Sheenish.

lessons.title: Snaue as sheanse
lessons.summary: The young swimmer Skye Ferris and her coach Shaun Brannigan visit a sports science room in Liverpool, where Wayne Kinsella measures her heart rate frequency through the epidermis, tests her vision with the colours of the spectrum, shows a mathematical model of her stroke and talks about chromosomes; a doctor tells the hoarse Shaun to rest his larynx, and Wayne talks about the singularity in a black hole.
lessons.text:
Ta Skye Ferris snaue son Ellan Vannin. Laa dy row, hie ee marish e ynseyder Shaun Brannigan dys shamyr sheanse spoyrt ayns Lerphoyll. She Wayne Kinsella yn fer-sheanse 'sy shamyr.

Hoshiaght, ren Wayne menkid cree Skye y scrutaghey. “She menkid y chree cre cho mennick as ta'n cree gleashaghey,” dooyrt eh. Hug eh red beg er y chrackan eck. “Ta'n red shoh er yn epiderm,” dooyrt eh. “She yn epiderm y crackan sodjey magh. Ta'n red clashtyn yn cree trooid yn epiderm.” Ren Skye snaue, as va menkid y chree eck er y cho-earrooder.

Eisht ren Wayne prowal reayrtagh. Va soilshaghyn jeh dagh daah 'sy spectrum er y cho-earrooder: jiarg, buigh, glass as gorrym. “Ta'n spectrum ooilley ayns soilshey yn ghrian,” dooyrt Wayne. Va feme ec Skye e laue y hroggal tra honnick ee soilshey gorrym. Va'n prowal reayrtagh aashagh: va sooillyn mie ec Skye.

Va jalloo maddaghtoil er y cho-earrooder myrgeddin. “Shoh cummey maddaghtoil jeh dty laueyn 'syn ushtey,” dooyrt Wayne. “Ta'n cummey maddaghtoil jeeaghyn dooin cre'n aght foddee oo snaue ny s'tappee.”

“Ta kroymasoomyn ayns dagh killag 'sy chorp,” dooyrt Wayne. “Ta ny kroymasoomyn veih dty ayr as veih dty voir. Agh cha nel ny kroymasoomyn agh paart jeh. Ta obbyr chrooaght scanshoil myrgeddin.” Va Skye breeoil: v'ee laccal snaue reesht. “T'ou feer vreeoil jiu!” dooyrt Shaun.

Va peesh dy phabyr er laue Skye. “Giar ersooyl eh,” dooyrt Shaun. Va'n pabyr giarit ersooyl ec Wayne.

Cha row Shaun abyl loayrt dy ard. Ren eh eam dy ard ec ny gammanyn snaue. Hie eh dys y fer-lheihys 'sy thie cheddin. “Ta drogh stayd er yn aahjioogh ayd,” dooyrt y fer-lheihys. “Ny jean eam son shiaghtin, as bee'n aahjioogh mie reesht.”

Er y voalley 'sy shamyr, va jalloo jeh towl doo. Ta Wayne studeyrys er towlyn doo myrgeddin. “Ta neuchadjinys ayns cree towl doo,” dooyrt eh. “Cha nel fys ec fer-sheanse erbee cre ta ayns y neuchadjinys.”

Feyshtyn:
Raad hie Skye as Shaun?
Hie ad dys shamyr sheanse spoyrt ayns Lerphoyll.
Cre ta menkid y chree?
She menkid y chree cre cho mennick as ta'n cree gleashaghey.
Cre ta yn epiderm?
She yn epiderm y crackan sodjey magh.
Cre va er y cho-earrooder 'sy phrowal reayrtagh?
Va soilshaghyn jeh dagh daah 'sy spectrum.
Cre dooyrt y fer-lheihys rish Shaun?
Dooyrt eh nagh lhisagh eh eam son shiaghtin.

lessons.title: Shooyl ayns Eeslynn
lessons.summary: Jordan Hurley and Callie Garvey travel to Iceland to walk among volcanic hills: tourists everywhere, low temperatures, a good transport system, and a walk up the edge of a glacier, where Callie shows good sense and turns back before a storm.
lessons.text:
Ta Jordan Hurley as Callie Garvey goll dy shooyl er ny sleityn dagh Jesarn ayns Ellan Vannin. 'Sy tourey shoh, ren ad troailt gys Eeslynn. Va'n troailt foddey: hie ad er etlan veih Lerphoyll.

Ayns Eeslynn, va ram turrysee. Va turrysee ayns ny shappyn, er ny raaidyn as ec dagh ynnyd aalin. “Ta shin turrysee myrgeddin,” dooyrt Callie, “agh ta shin turrysee ta shooyl.”

Ta Eeslynn ny ellan volcaanagh. Ta ny sleityn volcaanagh, as ta'n thalloo doo. Va ushtey çheh çheet seose ass y thalloo volcaanagh. Hie Jordan as Callie dy shooyl eddyr ny sleityn.

Va'n tempreilys injil 'sy tourey. 'Sy voghrey, va'n tempreilys ec queig keimyn. Ren Jordan jeeaghyn er y tempreilys er e çhellvane dagh moghrey.

Ta corys arraghee mie ayns Eeslynn. Ta gleashtanyn mooarey goll dys dagh balley. Tra va'n gheay feer lajer, ghow ad gleashtan mooar. “Ta'n corys arraghee shoh feer vie,” dooyrt Jordan.

Lurg shiaght laa, haink ad gys rio mooar. Va'n rio ayns glion eddyr daa slieau, as va'n creeagh echey bunnys gorrym. Va'n raad goll seose er creeagh y rio.

“Lhig dooin goll seose,” dooyrt Jordan. Agh va keeayll ec Callie. Honnick ee bodjallyn doo. “Ta geay lajer as fliaghey çheet,” dooyrt ee. “Ta keeayll ayns goll erash.” Hie ad erash, as haink y fliaghey lurg lieh oor. “Va keeayll ayd,” dooyrt Jordan.

Feyshtyn:
Raad ren Jordan as Callie troailt?
Ren ad troailt gys Eeslynn.
Quoi va ayns ny shappyn as er ny raaidyn?
Va ram turrysee ayn.
Cre'n sorçh dy ellan eh Eeslynn?
She ellan volcaanagh eh.
Cre va'n tempreilys 'sy voghrey?
Va'n tempreilys ec queig keimyn.
Cre'n fa hie ad erash?
Va keeayll ec Callie: va geay lajer as fliaghey çheet.

lessons.title: Yn refrane
lessons.summary: Tynwald holds a referendum on Wednesday on a new swimming pool in Douglas to replace the old one, once heated with coal; the reporter Kenzie Doherty writes for a sports paper with a large readership, the island's swimming organisation backs the plan, an angry man makes a complaint and threatens the builders, the police come, the government cuts the plan down, and Kenzie relaxes with a novel about a murder.
lessons.text:
Ta Kenzie Doherty ny screeudeyr. T'ee screeu son pabyr-naight spoyrt ayns Doolish. Ta lhaihderaght vooar ec y pabyr: ta mysh jeih thousane dy leih lhaih eh dagh shiaghtin. Ta'n lhaihderaght shen laccal naight mychione spoyrt 'syn ellan.

'Sy vee shoh, va Kenzie screeu mychione refrane. Ta'n reiltys laccal thie-snaue noa y hroggal ayns Doolish. Ta'n shenn thie-snaue feer shenn. Roish keead blein, va'n ushtey jeant çheh lesh geayl. Cha nel sleih jannoo ymmyd jeh geayl nish, agh ta'n thie-snaue dorraghey foast veih'n geayl.

Bee'n refrane ayn Jecrean. Jecrean, bee sleih Ellan Vannin reih: thie-snaue noa, ny cha nel.

Ta commyn snaue 'syn ellan, as ta ny paitçhyn as ny sleih aegey snaue ayns y commyn. Ta'n commyn laccal y thie-snaue noa. Loayr Kenzie rish ben veih'n commyn. “Ta'n shenn thie-snaue ro veg,” dooyrt ee. “Ta feme ec y commyn er thie-snaue noa.”

Agh cha row dagh unnane laccal y plan. Ren dooinney cassid noi'n plan. Hug eh cassid gys y reiltys, as eisht cassid elley gys y pabyr. “Ta'n plan ro deyr,” dooyrt eh.

Laa dy row, haink y dooinney gys yn ynnyd raad va'n thie-snaue noa dy ve troggit. Ren eh baggyrt er ny deiney va gobbraghey ayn. “Cha bee thie-snaue noa er y thalloo shoh!” dooyrt eh, as ren eh baggyrt dy vrishey ny clagh. Va aggle er ny deiney, as ren ad y poleen y eam. Haink y poleen, as loayr ad rish y dooinney. Lurg tammylt, hie eh thie. Cha ren eh baggyrt er peiagh erbee reesht.

Eisht ren y reiltys y plan y injillaghey. Bee'n thie-snaue noa ny sloo, as bee eh ny sloo deyr. Va taitnys ec ram sleih ayns y plan injillit.

Jecrean, ren ny sleih reih. Hooar y plan yn chooid smoo jeh ny reihyn. Screeu Kenzie art mychione y refrane son y lhaihderaght eck.

'Syn oie, ren Kenzie noaskeeal y lhaih. She skeeal mychione dunverys v'ayn: ayns y noaskeeal, ta'n poleen shirrey yn dooinney ren y dunverys. “She red aashagh eh dunverys ayns lioar,” dooyrt ee. “Ta refrane ny smoo doillee!”

Feyshtyn:
Son cre ta Kenzie screeu?
T'ee screeu son pabyr-naight spoyrt ayns Doolish.
Cre'n laa va'n refrane?
Va'n refrane Jecrean.
Cre va jannoo yn ushtey çheh 'sy shenn thie-snaue?
Va'n ushtey jeant çheh lesh geayl.
Cre ren y dooinney noi'n plan?
Ren eh cassid noi'n plan, as ren eh baggyrt er ny deiney.
Cre ren y reiltys lesh y plan?
Ren y reiltys y plan y injillaghey.

lessons.title: Yn fine
lessons.summary: At an archery club at Castle Rushen that re-enacts the old days of the Lordship of Mann, when the Dukes of Atholl from a Scottish dukedom held the island, the preacher Elijah Sheard keeps a secret in his quiver: a ring on a red thread; among the decorations he recites a verse of an old song and makes a proposal to Abigail Rooney.
lessons.text:
Ta club ayns Balley Chashtal raad ta sleih ceau sideyn lesh bow, myr ayns ny shenn laghyn. Dagh blein, ta'n club aachroo laa veih'n traa shen ec Cashtal Rushen. Ta ny olteyn ceau eaddagh shenn, as t'ad aachroo yn ceau sideyn as ny feaillaghyn.

Ta'n laa mychione çhiarnys Vannin. Ayns ny shenn laghyn, va çhiarnys yn ellan ec lught-thie Stanley. Eisht hie'n çhiarnys gys lught-thie Atholl. Ta diucaght Atholl ayns Nalbin. Va Çhiarn Vannin veih'n diucaght shen derrey 1765, tra hie'n çhiarnys gys Ree Hostyn.

Ta Abigail Rooney as Elijah Sheard ayns y club. She sushtallagh eh Elijah: t'eh loayrt mychione y Vible ayns agglish veg ayns Balley Chashtal. “She sushtallagh mie eh,” ta sleih yn agglish gra.

'Sy vlein shoh, va folliaght ec Elijah. Va fine er e ghreeym, lane dy sideyn. Agh ayns y fine, fo ny sideyn, va fainey beg. Va'n fainey er snaie jiarg, as va'n snaie kianglt rish y fine. Cha row fys ec Abigail er y folliaght.

Va jesheenyn er boallaghyn y chashtal: blaaghyn, eaddagh daahit as ny cowraghyn jeh Ellan Vannin. Va jesheen aalin er y voalley ard ec y chashtal, as va'n sleih jeeaghyn er y jesheen.

Lurg y ceau sideyn, haink ny olteyn ooilley dys y vagher. Hass Elijah fo ny jesheenyn. Dooyrt eh rane jeh arrane shenn. Va'n rane mychione graih, as va taitnys mooar ec ny sleih tra va'n rane ec y jerrey.

Eisht ghow Elijah yn snaie ass y fine, as va'n fainey er y snaie. Ren eh treealtys da Abigail. “Nee oo poosey mee?” dooyrt eh. “Nee!” dooyrt Abigail. Va'n treealtys aalin, as va'n folliaght ersooyl.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta'n club aachroo dagh blein?
T'eh aachroo laa veih ny shenn laghyn ec Cashtal Rushen.
Raad ta diucaght Atholl?
Ta diucaght Atholl ayns Nalbin.
Quoi eh Elijah Sheard?
She sushtallagh eh, as t'eh ayns y club.
Cre va ayns y fine echey?
Va fainey er snaie jiarg ayns y fine.
Cre ren Elijah lurg y rane?
Ren eh treealtys da Abigail.
